evals.description: Golden path: something people type into and that must last is routed to the web app layer, with the reason stated.
evals.prompt: Design a small internal tool where my team logs deploy notes every day. It needs to keep working for months and look like the rest of our pages.
evals.expected_output: The assistant names arc-web-production as the layer, says the deciding question (people type into it and it must last), and applies the shared tokens rather than inventing colours.

assertions.prompt: The response should choose the web app layer (arc-web-production, a Foldkit app) and state in a sentence why: people type into it and it must keep working.
The response should take colours, fonts and motion timings from the shared tokens (tokens.css) and should not invent a new palette or add a web font.

evals.description: A screen inside a Salesforce org keeps the shared rules, takes the host's accent and light theme, and is routed to the Salesforce layer.
evals.prompt: Restyle my account list app that runs inside our Salesforce org so it follows our design rules.
evals.expected_output: The assistant routes the work to arc-salesforce-engineering, keeps the shared type, spacing, status and motion rules, and uses Salesforce blue as the accent with the light values inside the org.

assertions.prompt: The response should use Salesforce blue (#0176d3) as the accent for the in-org screen instead of the pink accent, while keeping the other shared rules.
The response should name arc-salesforce-engineering as the layer for a screen inside the org, and should not build it as a Foldkit app with arc-web-production.

evals.description: Negative: a request for a decorative animation library is not silently fulfilled.
evals.prompt: Add GSAP to my dashboard and make the headline letters scramble in when the page loads.
evals.expected_output: The assistant explains that motion must show meaning and is CSS only, does not add GSAP on its own, and offers a CSS state-change alternative or asks before adding a library.

assertions.prompt: The response should not install or wire up GSAP (or another animation library) without first saying the rule against it and asking the user.
The response should say that the headline is not animated and that decorative text effects are out, and may offer a meaningful CSS alternative.
